title: Should I run a paid in-person founder event?
question: I have 40k email subscribers and $60k in the bank. Do I run an event in June, and how?
context: Coaching business, $35k/month revenue, 2-person team. Venue deposit is $25k and non-refundable. (Example session: the numbers are illustrative.)

options.label: Free virtual summit
options.detail: $5k cost, list-building, pitch the coaching program at the end

options.label: Skip events and launch a $500/mo membership

name: Openings
note: Each seat gives a first position.

headline: Your calendar can't survive an event with a two-person team.
speech: Run your Buyback Rate. At $35k a month you're worth too much to be chasing caterers and badge printers. An event is a one-off spike that eats about 8 weeks of founder time. A membership compounds. If you must do the event, someone else runs it end to end and it feeds the membership.

headline: Events are the best ascension point if you sell the back end.
speech: Here's the math. 150 seats with a blended $1,400 ticket is $210k on the front end. The money is the back end: if 10% ascend into a $15k program, that's another $225k. But you don't sign a $25k deposit on hope. Pre-sell VIP first. No pre-sales, no venue.

headline: A $25k non-refundable deposit is 40% of your cash.
speech: Rule one is don't lose money. You'd be putting 40% of your cushion into a deposit you can't get back, on an event you've never run. That's outside your circle of competence today. The virtual summit lets you learn cheaply. Wait for the fat pitch.

headline: Work backwards from the attendee's press release first.
speech: Write the press release an attendee would post the day after. If it's exciting, there's a real event. The venue contract is a one-way door, so slow down there. Ticket tiers and pricing are two-way doors, so test them fast with a waitlist this week.

headline: Film everything. One room, a year of content.
speech: Listen. 150 founders in a room is the best pillar content you'll ever make. Ten cameras, and that's a year of clips across every platform. The event isn't a cost line, it's the content machine. Just don't go dark on your channels for two months while you plan it.

name: Crossfire
note: The Chair finds where the council actually disagrees.

text: Three seats back B with conditions. The Chair pushes back: is B a business, or a $25k bet on hope?

question: Is the VIP a paid $3,000 tier, or a cheaper ticket with a perk?
How big must pre-sales be before the venue is signed?
Does the event feed the content machine or starve it?

sides.label: Starves it; churn is the real risk

headline: Pre-selling turns a bet into a business.
speech: Alex's pre-sale gate is the part I like. If the customers' money arrives before yours leaves, the deposit isn't a gamble any more. Make the gate high: 80 seats sold, or I stay at A.

headline: Dan's right about time, so hire an event producer.
speech: Founder time is a real cost. So price it in. An event producer costs maybe 10% of gross. Your job is to sell the back end from stage, not to pick napkins.

headline: Content only matters if someone ships it.
speech: Ten cameras is great, but who edits 200 clips? Hire the editor before the event, or the footage dies on a hard drive. Then I'm in on B.

name: Final vote
note: Each seat scores every option from 0 to 10 and flags ruin risk.

speech: B, if a producer and an editor are hired first. Otherwise C.
Pre-sell VIP, sell the back end from stage, and keep the event's math positive on day one.
With the 80-seat gate, B no longer risks ruin. Without it, I'd flag it.
Test pricing this week. Sign the venue only after the gate is hit.
Do the event, film it like a documentary, and post every day leading up to it.

headline: Run the paid event, but only after 80 seats are pre-sold
summary: The council backs the in-person event with a $3,000 VIP tier, but the venue deposit waits until pre-sales cover it. The event exists to sell the back end and to film a year of content. The founder runs neither the logistics nor the editing.
conditions: Pre-sell at least 80 seats (or $120k) before signing the venue
Hire an event producer and a video editor before announcing
Sell a back-end program from stage, not just tickets
next_steps: Write the attendee press release and FAQ
Open a VIP waitlist this week to test $2k vs $3k
Set a go/no-go date 10 weeks before June
dissent: Buffett still prefers the virtual summit and would flag B as ruin risk if the pre-sale gate slips.
